clue.text: Cold sort of teacher, head showing ill temper

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
a ness is a headland, as in Sheerness

explanation.surface: A chilly schoolteacher, the head no less, displaying a nasty mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a head teacher, but it is a geographical head, a promontory, which is NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crabby is being grumpy and irritable, so the noun means a bad-tempered mood.

clue.text: African Christian is nabbed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it sounds spoken

parts.note: copped is slang for caught or nabbed

explanation.surface: A Christian from Africa is arrested, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Copts are members of the Coptic Church, the ancient Christian church of Egypt.

clue.text: Socially awkward types ask to be moved when girl comes in

indicators.note: comes in means the girl's name goes inside the rearranged letters
to be moved means the letters of ask are shifted into a new order

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Awkward people request a change of seat when a woman enters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' suggests people changing seats, but 'to be moved' is the anagram signal, giving AKS, and 'comes in' is the container signal for the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks is British slang for obsessive, socially inept enthusiasts, after the hooded jackets of trainspotters.

clue.text: Requirement for a jet-setter to get on?

definitions.text: Requirement for a jet-setter to get on?

parts.words: Requirement for a jet-setter to get on?
parts.note: a frequent flyer needs a document to be allowed onto the plane

explanation.surface: What a high-flyer needs to succeed in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' suggests getting ahead in society, but it means literally boarding the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines issue a document that every passenger must show before boarding the plane.

clue.text: Close thing in inlet, one in loch

indicators.note: in means the inlet and one go inside the loch's name

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake
an arm of the sea is an inlet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A narrow escape somewhere on the waters of a Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or something that very nearly happened is called a close shave or close call.

clue.text: Reticent to admit sin produced by drink

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the shy word takes another inside

parts.note: shy means reserved, reticent
to err is to sin, to go astray

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to confess a wrongdoing brought on by alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain is a classic aperitif drink.

clue.text: Fashionable little bird losing its tail

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

explanation.surface: A stylish fledgling that has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a synonym for stylish, smart and in vogue.

clue.text: A laugh about English type of transport

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of a laugh are moved around

explanation.surface: A joke concerning an English method of getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the business of carrying goods by road, a kind of freight transport.

clue.text: Restrictions ripped apart in retail outlet

parts.note: chains are restraints, restrictions
tore means ripped apart

explanation.surface: Rules torn up inside a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped apart' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym, TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a group of shops under the same ownership and branding is a retail outlet.

clue.text: Broadcast supporting the old man not allowed out

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man
a gated pupil or student is confined to the premises

explanation.surface: A broadcast in support of a father who has been grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seeds or ideas is to spread them widely, which is to propagate them.

clue.text: Wild animal turning up in the morning rolled over

indicators.note: turning means the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rolled over means the abbreviation for morning is turned round too

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A wild beast shows up at dawn and rolls on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed separately: 'turning' turns UP into PU, and 'rolled over' turns AM into MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a big wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Portraits once briefly roughed out for series of drawings

indicators.note: roughed out means sketched loosely, so the letters are put down in a new arrangement
briefly means the word once is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Portraits that were once quickly sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' turns ONCE into ONC; those letters join PORTRAITS for the anagram signalled by 'roughed out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip in a newspaper is a sequence of cartoon panels telling a story.

clue.text: Boy eating beefburger ultimately becoming fat

indicators.note: eating means the boy's word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of beefburger is used

explanation.surface: A lad who scoffs burgers ends up overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat rendered for cooking.

clue.text: Author's holy book I want badly

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament, one of the Gospels

indicators.note: badly means the letters of I want are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A writer badly wants a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'has': the author has the holy book followed by the rearranged letters of 'I want'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer of Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn wrote under this pen name.

clue.text: What could be going or gone as part of our language

definitions.text: What could be going or gone as part of our language

parts.words: What could be going or gone as part of our language
parts.note: going and gone are the two verb forms used in tenses and as adjectives, present and past

explanation.surface: Words that are disappearing from English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going or gone' suggests words dying out, but they are grammatical forms of the verb go.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb form ending in -ing or -ed/-en used in compound tenses and as an adjective is this part of speech.

clue.text: Criminal taken in by parson is transformed

indicators.note: taken in by says the answer sits inside the run of words parson is transformed

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is taken in by a clergyman and reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are simply hidden: p(ARSON IS T)ransformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately sets fire to property commits a crime, so is a criminal.

clue.text: Djibouti's leading character is this

parts.note: the D at the start of the African country's name is not pronounced

explanation.surface: A remark about the leader of the African state of Djibouti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' suggests a national leader, but it is the first letter of the word, D, which goes unspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter not pronounced, like the D in the country name, is described as mute.

clue.text: Company problem involving male, a sort of 'key worker'?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the male letter goes inside

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A firm's difficulty involving a man who is an essential worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key worker' sounds like an essential employee, but a musician writing in a key is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music works in musical keys, so is jokingly a worker with keys.

clue.text: Strikes — so politician must get stuck in

indicators.note: must get stuck in means the politician is placed inside the word for so

parts.note: thus means so, therefore
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Industrial action, so an MP has to roll up their sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' looks like industrial action, but it is the verb: hits hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump something is to hit it heavily, so it is a synonym for strikes as a verb.

clue.text: It's not grand for a pianist to play

definitions.text: It's not grand for a pianist to play

parts.words: It's not grand for a pianist to play
parts.note: a piano that is not the large horizontal concert kind is the vertical household type

explanation.surface: A modest instrument for a musician to perform on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' reads as 'splendid', but it is the grand piano; the other main type stands vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano with vertical strings in a tall case is the common alternative to a grand.

clue.text: More sensitive, suppressing expression of pain in row

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
ouch is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone thin-skinned stifling a cry of pain during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone touchy is easily offended, so the comparative means more easily upset.

clue.text: State of Asian country area

parts.note: Indian means of or from India, the Asian country

explanation.surface: The condition of an area in a country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of' looks like it means 'condition of', but 'State' alone is the US state and 'of Asian country' gives INDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a midwestern US state with Indianapolis as its capital.

clue.text: Wise person carrying English Bible — hoping to convert me?

definitions.note: the definition is the person a missionary wants to convert, speaking as me

indicators.note: carrying means the wise person's word holds the Bible's abbreviation inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible in English

explanation.surface: A wise man carries a Bible to win over a heathen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the convert-to-be: a missionary with a Bible hopes to convert him, in old colonial thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Missionaries of old saw so-called uncivilised people as targets for conversion to Christianity.

clue.text: Cheat who may have a heart hidden away?

definitions.text: Cheat who may have a heart hidden away?

parts.words: Cheat who may have a heart hidden away?
parts.note: a playing card of the hearts suit could be hidden up the sleeve of a dishonest player

explanation.surface: A deceiver who secretly has a kind heart after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' reads as kindness, but it is a card from the hearts suit kept up a sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional swindler at card games may keep a card concealed to play when needed.

clue.text: Seaside town journey being reported

indicators.note: being reported means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a ride is a journey, as on a bus or horse

explanation.surface: A trip to the coast that is being written up.
explanation.walkthrough: RYDE is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a resort town on the Isle of Wight, reached by ferry and hovercraft.

clue.text: Turn taking bishop to close

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a close is an end, a conclusion

explanation.surface: A cleric takes his turn to bring things to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bend is a curve or turn in a road or river.

clue.text: Servant in front half of magnificent parades

indicators.note: front half of means only the first half of the word's letters are kept

parts.note: pageants are splendid processions or spectacles

explanation.surface: A servant leading the procession at a grand parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A page was a boy attendant or servant to a knight or noble household.

clue.text: Eager to proceed, I had to carry on

parts.note: to pass is to go on, proceed

indicators.note: to carry means the I and the word for had hold another word between them

parts.note: had, as in had dinner, means ate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keen to get going, I had to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' looks like a phrase meaning continue, but 'to carry' is the container signal and 'on' is the piece carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen and intense about something is ardent, enthusiastic, eager.

clue.text: Amphibians — not all left stranded

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Creatures of pond and land, some of them stranded on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are amphibians, and an eft is an old or dialect word for a newt.

clue.text: Sound excellent in cranium — due to this?

definitions.text: Sound excellent in cranium — due to this?

indicators.note: in means the sound and the excellent piece are placed inside the cranium word

parts.note: the cranium is the skull, the head
to ring is to sound, as a bell does
A1 means first-rate, excellent; the 1 is read as I

explanation.surface: Someone hard of hearing finds sounds crystal clear thanks to a small device.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the device makes sound excellent inside one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A small electronic device worn in the ear amplifies sound for those with impaired hearing.
